summary: Across 11 completed experiments, 217.1 minutes of wall time included 6 compute-bound experiments. The slowest compute-bound entries took 77.78, 47.45, and 22.3 minutes; the timing record provides no phase-level causes for those durations.
bottlenecks_identified: The two longest recorded experiments were compute-bound, but the timing record contains no phase-level data to explain their durations.
Milestone timing required disk-mtime reconstruction after the live git-log path found no commits, limiting stage-level attribution.
No task-correlated GPU samples or model-concurrency receipts are available, so compute-bound GPU efficiency and runner selection cannot be diagnosed beyond the locked false idle indicator.
improvements_suggested: Emit per-experiment phase timers for setup, model loading, inference, verification, and reconciliation so the next slow path has a measured cause.
Record task-correlated GPU utilization with the active task, compute-bound classification, model count, and selected runner in one timing receipt.
Select DualGPURunner automatically only for declared multi-model parallel work, while retaining the single-GPU path for single-model inference.
top_3_highest_leverage_actions: Add phase-level timing receipts to every experiment artifact.
Correlate GPU telemetry with active compute-bound task boundaries.
Add model-concurrency-aware runner selection and record the selection decision.
meta_reflection: The available data supports ranking slow experiments but not assigning causal explanations or a nonzero savings estimate. The next retrospective will become actionable if timing, GPU activity, model concurrency, and runner choice are captured in the same task-scoped record.
